script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

A sea of students, all chatting amongst themselves, eating their lunches. At one table, sits JANE, a thirty-something woman, staring down at her untouched sandwich.

JANE (V.O.)
(sighing)
Five more days until retirement. Five more days until I can finally leave this hellhole behind.

Suddenly, the room falls silent as the principal's voice echoes through the intercom.

PRINCIPAL (V.O.)
Attention all students and staff. We have a surprise visitor today. He's a renowned author, a former teacher of this very school, and he's here to speak to you all. Please join me in the auditorium for this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

Jane puts down her sandwich, and as she stands up to leave, a young boy, MIKE, bumps into her tray, spilling its contents all over the floor.

MIKE (whispering, eyes wide)
Oh no, I'm so sorry!

Jane looks down at her ruined lunch in disgust before storming off, muttering to herself.

INT. AUDITORIUM - DAY

The auditorium is filled with students and teachers, all eager to meet the famous author. Jane enters last, grumbling to herself. As she takes a seat in the back row, she notices the author, ROBERT, sitting on the stage.

ROBERT
(smiling)
Hello everyone, I'm Robert. You may know me from my novels, "The Second Chance" and "Finding Forgiveness."

The crowd claps politely. Jane rolls her eyes, unimpressed.

Robert continues.

ROBERT
I used to teach here many years ago, and I have to say, it brings back a flood of memories. Many of which are quite fond. I remember a young student named Jane. She was always so sharp and quick-witted. I knew she'd go far in life.

Jane looks up, her eyes wide with shock. Robert smiles and waves at her, gesturing for her to come up to the stage.

JANE (stammering)
Me? Why me?

Robert nods.

ROBERT
Yes, you. I'd like you to share a story with the class about a time in your life when you were given a second chance.

Jane hesitates, but eventually makes her way to the stage. She takes a deep breath before beginning her story.

INT. JANE'S KITCHEN - FLASHBACK

Jane, looking younger and more carefree, sits at the kitchen table with her best friend, MARK. They are eating ice cream and laughing.

JANE (laughing)
I can't believe I got away with that one!

MARK
(smiling)
You always do, Jane. You're just too clever for your own good.

The door bursts open, and in storms JANE'S MOTHER.

JANE'S MOTHER
(furious)
Jane! How could you do this to me? I trusted you!

Jane looks down, guilt written all over her face. Mark puts a comforting hand on her shoulder.

MARK
It's okay, Jane. We'll figure this out.

INT. COURTROOM - FLASHBACK

Jane, now in her late twenties, sits in a courtroom, looking pale and afraid. The judge bangs his gavel.

JUDGE
The court finds the defendant, Jane, guilty of embezzlement and theft. You will serve five years in prison.

Jane weeps as the courtroom clears out, leaving her alone with her thoughts.

INT. PRISON - FLASHBACK

Five years later, Jane sits in a prison cell, her spirit broken. But then, she receives a letter. It's from Robert, offering her a job as his assistant when she's released.

JANE (V.O.)
(reading)
"Dear Jane, I've heard about what's happened to you, and I'm here to offer you a second chance. When you're released, come work for me. I believe in you, Jane."

INT. AUDITORIUM - PRESENT

Jane finishes her story, her voice shaking with emotion. The room falls silent, then erupts in applause. Robert smiles at her, proud.

ROBERT
That was a beautiful story, Jane. I'm glad you got a second chance. And I hope that, no matter what happens in life, you never give up on yourself.

Jane nods, tears in her eyes. She takes a deep breath, feeling a renewed sense of hope.

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
